Unit.UnitTitle: Unit 4: The Integration Object – Mastering the Ecosystem

Session.Title: 4.1 The Integration Object: Scaling Modular Power

Section.Title: Beyond the Hello World
Section.Paragraph: In the previous units, we mastered the Blueprint and the Artifact. But real software exists in ecosystems. Unit 4 introduces the Integration Object—where multiple modular artifacts combine into a functional, high-stakes system.

Our case study is LNbits, a Bitcoin Lightning Network system. By applying our Nix/uv foundations, we build extensions that are perfectly reproducible, even when relying on complex backends like Bitcoin nodes.

Section.Title: Modular Synergy
Section.Paragraph: Instead of a "monolithic" application, we think of the system as a Composition:

BulletedList.ListItem: Backend: The LNbits core (managed as a Nix input).

Section.Paragraph: This encapsulation ensures that changes to the core do not break the extension, as dependencies never "leak" between objects.

Question.Paragraph: To complete the course, launch the Unit 4 Laboratory.
1. Navigate to the laboratory folder: ou_tm470/oer/lab/unit4_integration/.
2. Run nix develop to enter the integrated environment.
3. Launch the LNbits instance and verify the Scrum extension is active.
How does the "Integration Object" approach improve the stability of complex software like LNbits?

Answer.Paragraph: By treating each component (Core, Extension, Node) as an encapsulated object with its own immutable dependencies, we prevent Dependency Hell. We can update individual pieces of the stack with confidence, knowing they won't interfere with the system state of other components.

Paragraph.Emphasis: Pedagogical Note: Unit 4 represents the "Synthesis" phase of Tait’s framework, where granular concepts are integrated into a meaningful, functional whole.
